newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money trades unchanged at 3.00/03 pct.
newsitem.headline: German call money trades unchanged at 3.00/03 pct.

text.p: German call money rates traded mostly unchanged on Tuesday at rates close to the three percent repo rate, having digested the glut of liquidity injected at the end of last month.

Rates again traded between 3.00/03 percent on Tuesday, the rate which has prevailed in the money market for several months. At the end of May rates dipped had below 2.50 percent as the market was awash with excess funds.

On Tuesday dealers said liquidity conditions were quite ample, judging by the monthly reserve data which showed commercial banks holding 44.6 billion marks in non-interest bearing accounts on Monday. This compares with 42.9 billion marks held a day earlier.
The monthly average climbed to 43.7 billion marks from 41.3 billion marks and banks borrowed 100 million marks at the emergency Lombard borrowing facility.
Dealers said that in light of ample liquidity conditions, the Bundesbank might be inclined to drain funds at this week's auction.
The Bundesbank this morning set tenders for a 14-day securities repurchase funds, offering banks liquidity at a fixed three percent rate.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average was set at 3.03733 percent on Tuesday after 3.05000 on Monday.
